root_cause.text: In the RDMA mlx4 SRQ creation error path, mlx4_ib_create_srq() failed to unwind the hardware SRQ allocation by not calling mlx4_srq_free() after a successful mlx4_srq_alloc() when a later ib_copy_to_udata() step failed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the ib_copy_to_udata() failure branch from `goto err_wrid;` to `goto err_srq;` and adds `err_srq: mlx4_srq_free(dev->dev, &srq->msrq);`, while the commit message explicitly states that “mlx4_srq_alloc() was not undone during error unwind, add the missing call to mlx4_srq_free().”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes the ib_copy_to_udata() failure branch from `goto err_wrid;` to `goto err_srq;` and adds `err_srq: mlx4_srq_free(dev->dev, &srq->msrq);`, while the commit message explicitly states that “mlx4_srq_alloc() was not undone during error unwind, add the missing call to mlx4_srq_free().”

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the allocated SRQ when ib_copy_to_udata() fails to avoid leaking SRQ resources during SRQ creation error handling.
intent_record.what: The error path after a failed ib_copy_to_udata() call was changed from jumping directly to err_wrid to jumping to a new err_srq label, and a call to mlx4_srq_free(dev->dev, &srq->msrq) was added at that new label before continuing to the existing cleanup path.
intent_record.how: When copying the SRQ number to user data fails, the function now frees the previously allocated SRQ object before unmapping the user doorbell resources, preventing the SRQ allocation from being leaked on this error path.

grouping_result.intent: Free the allocated SRQ when ib_copy_to_udata() fails to avoid leaking SRQ resources during SRQ creation error handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the described root cause by freeing the previously allocated SRQ on the ib_copy_to_udata() failure path, preventing the SRQ resource leak during mlx4_ib_create_srq() error handling.

candidates.rationale: On ib_copy_to_udata() failure, control jumps to an error path that does not free the already allocated hardware SRQ via mlx4_srq_free(), directly causing the SRQ resource leak.
This is the failing post-allocation step whose error handling is incomplete; after successful mlx4_srq_alloc(), this branch leads into cleanup that omits freeing the hardware SRQ.
This error label denotes the cleanup path reached after ib_copy_to_udata() failure, and that path lacked mlx4_srq_free(), making it the locus of the unwind bug.

vuln_statements.explanation: After successful hardware SRQ allocation, this jump routes ib_copy_to_udata() failure into an error path that did not call mlx4_srq_free(), causing the SRQ resource leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is fully visible in mlx4_ib_create_srq(), so the snippet is sufficient. After successful hardware SRQ allocation via `err = mlx4_srq_alloc(dev->dev, to_mpd(pd)->pdn, &srq->mtt, srq->db.dma, &srq->msrq); if (err) goto err_wrid;`, the user path performs `if (pd->uobject) if (ib_copy_to_udata(udata, &srq->msrq.srqn, sizeof (__u32))) { err = -EFAULT; goto err_wrid; }`. On this failure, control goes to `err_wrid:` which only does `mlx4_ib_db_unmap_user(...)` or `kfree(srq->wrid);`, then `err_mtt:` does `mlx4_mtt_cleanup(...)`, and later frees buffer/db/srq. There is no call to `mlx4_srq_free(dev->dev, &srq->msrq)` anywhere in this error path. The only `mlx4_srq_free()` in the file is in `mlx4_ib_destroy_srq()`, which is not reached during create failure. Therefore the function contains the vulnerable construct: it allocates the hardware SRQ and, if `ib_copy_to_udata()` fails afterward, it leaks/unwinds incorrectly by not freeing the allocated SRQ. The fix is not present because the post-allocation error path lacks `mlx4_srq_free()`.
